Omar (customer): Hey team — started seeing a cluster of 429s + occasional 500s yesterday evening after a big traffic spike. Latency also jumped from ~120ms to 700-1500ms for some requests. We're on the hosted API, single API key. Suspect quota or some throttling. No changes on our side.
Elena G: Sorry you're hit with this, Omar. Can you paste one raw request/response (headers) and the route + model you called? Also rough QPS and concurrency during the spike?
Omar (customer): here's a minimal curl we used during repro:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REPLACE' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"rw-large-1","input":"summarize: ...","max_tokens":256}'
```
And sample response headers we captured (truncated):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Redwood-Limit: 12000
X-Redwood-Remaining: 0
X-Redwood-Reset: 1672531200
X-Request-Id: rwd_abc123
Retry-After: 10
```
We were hitting ~35 concurrent requests for a 30s window, peak QPS ~110. Hit ratio on our side didn't change.
Jae L: Thanks, that header set is helpful. A couple of quick notes that often look like 'throttling' but are batching/cache interactions: 1) continuous batching can increase single-request P99 if the batcher is waiting for small inflight requests to fill a batch window, 2) KV-cache miss storms after a large, diverse burst can spike backend compute and cause transient quota exhaustion on shared pooled capacity.
Maya N: Yup. Seen this pattern: sudden fanout of distinct prefixes -> KV cache cold misses -> each request forces a heavier decode path + longer GPU time -> effective concurrency consumed -> upstream token quota/slot pool flips to deny new inflight requests. To triage: check batcher metrics and kvcache hit rate around the timestamps.
Elena G: Omar, can you share the route name (the exact API path you call) and the approx unix ts range of the spike? We'll pull request_id rwd_abc123 from logs. Also does your org have an autoscaling/dedicated plan? If not, you share pooled caps with other tenants which makes bursts more fragile.
Omar (customer): route is `/v1/generate` (default), spike window 2024-02-01 03:12:10 -> 03:13:10 UTC. We're on hosted free trial (no dedicated).
Jae L: Repro steps I recommend while we look: 1) Run a small test that keeps payload prefix identical for many parallel requests (to warm the KV cache). 2) Run the same QPS but capped concurrency (e.g., max 8 concurrent) to see if 429s stop. 3) Inspect response headers for `X-Redwood-Burst-Used` and `X-Redwood-Remaining` on each response.
Elena G: Also please try toggling client-side exponential backoff + jitter (start 200ms, factor 2) — a common mitigation: simple code snippet: `if (resp.status == 429) sleep(backoff); retry()`
Omar (customer): We tested reducing concurrency to 8 and the 429s disappeared, latency mostly back to normal. But we need to support short bursts — are there config knobs or recommended patterns on Redwood side?
Maya N: Short answer: yes. Two options: 1) request temporary burst increase / reserved slots while you ramp, or 2) change client-side strategy to smoothen the burst (queueing + bounded concurrency) and pre-warm KV cache. For hosted customers we can tune soft-burst allowances per API key; requires support ticket and short window.
ops-bot: Note: created infra-escalation ticket #INC-2024-412 and added eng-runtime.
Jae L: A deeper explanation: continuous batching groups many small incoming requests into multi-request GPU work for throughput efficiency. If the batcher waits up to X ms to fill a batch, some requests see higher latency. If you have many unique prefixes (low KV hit), GPU time per batch grows, reducing throughput and triggering rate limiting at the routing layer.
Jae L: Sharing an example of batcher stats we typically look for (from runtime logs):
```
batch_window_ms: 12
avg_batch_size: 18
p99_latency_batching_ms: 110
kvcache_hit_rate: 0.14
active_gpu_slots: 42/48
```
Low kvcache_hit_rate and high avg_batch_size + full GPU slots = danger zone.
Elena G: Short-term mitigations we applied for other customers: - Enable per-key burst allowance (gives you N extra concurrent slots for M minutes) - Lower max_batch_window_ms to reduce wait-for-fill (helps latency, may increase cost) - Pre-warm kvcache with synthetic requests before traffic ramp - Move to Dedicated / Reserved pool if predictable spikes are expected
Omar (customer): Any concrete config values you'd recommend for us to try?
Jae L: Try these client and server-side experiments: - client: cap concurrency to 12, add linear jittered backoff for 429s, make retries idempotent - server hints: set `max_batch_window_ms` -> 6 (from 12), `max_batch_tokens` -> 4096, enable prefix_warmup: true (if available), kvcache_eviction_threshold -> 0.6
Elena G: I'll open a support trial to enable a temporary per-key burst grant for your API key for 1 hour so you can absorb the next ramp while we investigate root cause. Also scheduling an eng-runtime review of logs.
billing-bot: Heads-up: burst grants still count against usage; if you go over the trial credits we will invoice overage per standard terms. Recommend setting an org alert at 80% quota.
Omar (customer): Thanks — the temp burst grant would've helped last night. We'll also implement the concurrency cap immediately. Please paste the follow-up steps you'll take so I can close internal incident.
Elena G: Follow-ups: 1) Support: enabled 1-hour burst grant for your API key (ticket INC-2024-412). 2) Eng-runtime: review rwd_abc123 and surrounding requests for 03:12:00-03:14:00 UTC to identify whether KV cache eviction or batch saturation caused the drop. 3) Ops: recommend dashboard alert on `X-Redwood-Remaining` trending to 0 and kvcache_hit_rate under 0.3. 4) Customer: implement concurrency cap + backoff; pre-warm prefixes if you have predictable burst inputs. 5) If repeat bursts expected, evaluate Dedicated capacity.
Maya N: I'll pull runtime logs and paste the relevant aggregation in this thread when ready. If we see repeated KV churn we should consider tuning eviction policy for hosted pool (eng-runtime decision).
Elena G: Closing loop — Omar, we'll post a short RCA in this thread within 48h. For now, the immediate action you should take: cap concurrency to 12 and add exponential backoff for 429s. Let us know after you run those tests. :thumbsup:
Omar (customer): Will do. Appreciate the fast help.
